study_identification_part.si4_title: Lifespan Normative Models of White Matter Fractional Anisotropy: Applications to Early Psychosis

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The introduction explicitly lists the aims: build lifespan FA normative models on >25,000 healthy individuals, apply them to early psychosis, perform multimodal fusion with cortical thickness/subcortical volumes to link to symptom domains, and release the models. These statements meet both criteria by describing research questions and the purpose of normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: The aims of this study are to: (i) develop normative models of Fractional Anisotropy (FA)… using a large dataset of over 25,000 healthy individuals… (ii) investigate white matter FA in early psychosis… (iii) …combine FA deviations with cortical thickness and subcortical brain volume deviations… identify multimodal biological signatures… (iv) we release all models freely to the community

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: They describe assembling high-quality multi-shell diffusion data from HCP and UK Biobank cohorts, report total N and train/test split, and note outlier exclusion (>5 SD) before refitting models. However, explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria or detailed image quality standards and exclusion reasons are not fully specified.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: we assembled high-quality multi-shell diffusion data from five cohorts… Total N=24,915 (N=12,457 for training and N=12,457 for test…)… processed using harmonised FSL-based pipelines… we refit the models after excluding gross outliers having deviations larger than 5 standard deviations from the mean

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The normative model explicitly includes age, sex, dummy-coded race, and site as covariates, addressing core demographics and site effects.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: A normative model was then fit… The model incorporated several covariates, including sex, age, and dummy coded race, and site.

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: They list the specific datasets used to build the reference cohort (HCP Baby, Development, Young Adult, Aging, UK Biobank) and provide demographic breakdowns in Supplementary Table S1.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: assembled high-quality multi-shell diffusion data from five cohorts… HCP Baby… HCP Development… HCP Young Adult… HCP Aging… and UK Biobank

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Image data come from existing large-scale cohorts (HCP and UK Biobank) rather than primary acquisition in this study; per guidance, acquisition protocol details are not required and are treated as not applicable.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: They describe harmonised preprocessing with FSL-based pipelines including B0 intensity normalization, distortion and motion corrections, DTIfit for FA estimation, TBSS skeletonization, and JHU atlas segmentation, indicating clear preprocessing steps.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: processed using harmonised FSL-based pipelines, involving preprocessing (intensity normalisation, distortion and movement corrections), DTI modelling to extract fractional anisotropy (FA) values, Tract-Based Spatial Statistics (TBSS)… segmentation with the Johns Hopkins University (JHU) atlas; pre-processing was performed: B0 intensity normalization, correction for EPI distortions, eddy-current-induced and movement corrections… estimated the DTI model using DTIfit… ran Tract-Based Spatial Statistics (TBSS)… segmentation… using the Johns Hopkins University (JHU) atlas

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They employed an internal split of the reference cohort into equal training and test sets (12,457 each) for model fitting and evaluation, satisfying the data partitioning strategy criterion.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: Total N=24,915, (N=12,457 for training and N=12,457 for test, stratified for sex, self-reported race, dataset and site)… splitting the dataset of subjects… into two equal groups: a test set… and a training set…

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study reports only the internal train/test split of the reference cohort and does not apply the normative model to an independent external healthy dataset for validation.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: split… into two equal groups: a test set… and a training set… (no mention of an external healthy validation cohort beyond this internal split)

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: They specify using warped Bayesian linear regression with a third-order B-spline basis over age, including covariates and describing the warping function, aligning with criteria for detailed statistical approach.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: we employed a warped Bayesian linear regression (BLR) model… applying a third-order polynomial B-spline basis expansion over age, with five evenly spaced knots, combined with a SinhArcsinh warping function.

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Model performance is quantified with explained variance, skewness, and kurtosis across tracts, providing quantitative fit metrics.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: We assessed the quality… using three key out-of-sample metrics, namely explained variance (EV)… skewness and kurtosis… The mean (standard deviation) EV was 0.37 (0.10)… Skewness… -0.09 (0.12) and 0.42 (0.27).

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: They report the sample sizes for training and test sets and note stratification by sex, race, dataset, and site, but do not provide detailed demographic summaries (e.g., age distributions) for each partition.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: Total N=24,915, (N=12,457 for training and N=12,457 for test, stratified for sex, self-reported race, dataset and site).

nm11_reproducibility.reason: They specify the software environment (Python 3.8, PCNtoolkit) and state model availability via open-source tools and a GitHub repository, addressing reproducibility and access.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: All statistical analyses were conducted using Python version 3.8, with the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience PCN toolkit (GitHub, PCNtoolkit); we provide these models to the field via our established no-code software platform… and via open-source software tools (https://github.com/ramonacirstian/fa_normative_modeling)

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: The clinical cohort source and diagnostic criteria are described (HCP-EP dataset; SCID-5 for early psychosis; sample sizes for patients/controls), and medication status was recorded. However, imaging quality criteria and exclusion reasons are not detailed.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: we applied the model to the Human Connectome Project Early Psychosis (HCP-EP) dataset… participants diagnosed with early psychosis (n=118) and control participants (n=55)… Participants with early psychosis were diagnosed using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-5 (SCID-5)… Medication status was also documented, including antipsychotic type and dosage…

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses link deviation scores to symptom domains via msCCA, but no clinical covariates beyond demographics (e.g., medication, illness duration) are incorporated into the deviation analyses; medication is only documented without being modeled.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: Symptom severity was quantified using the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS)… we combined FA deviations with cortical thickness and subcortical volume measures… to determine the multivariate association with symptoms, we used… msCCA… (see methods for details).

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: The study names the clinical dataset (HCP-EP) and describes the imaging modalities included (multi-shell diffusion and T1-weighted MRI).
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: we applied the model to the Human Connectome Project Early Psychosis (HCP-EP) dataset… which includes multi-shell diffusion data and T1-weighted structural MRI

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes, demographics (sex and race distributions), and symptom scores are provided for patients and controls in the methods text and Supplementary Table S2.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: participants diagnosed with early psychosis (n=118) and control participants (n=55)… The dataset's demographic distribution comprises 37% females and 63% males, with a racial composition of 58% White, 28% Black, 9% Asian, 1% Mixed, and 3% Other; Table S2 lists age, sex, race, and PANSS statistics

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Clinical assessments are specified: SCID-5 for diagnosis and PANSS (including Marder factor scores) for symptom severity, with mention of structured interview and symptom domains.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: Participants with early psychosis were diagnosed using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-5 (SCID-5)… symptoms assessed with the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS)… the positive symptom factor, negative symptom factor, cognitive/disorganised symptom factor in addition to the total PANSS score.

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: They define deviation score thresholds (|Z|>2.6) to classify extreme positive/negative deviations, report group differences in proportions, and discuss heterogeneity and symptom associations, satisfying explanation of meaning and clinical implications.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: extreme positive (Mann-Whitney U=1403.0, p=0.0036) and extreme negative (U=1517.0, p=0.0016) Z-scores… thresholds set at 2.6 and 2.6… indicating substantial differences… highlighting a consistent trend where patients exhibited a greater number of extreme Z-scores… and later association with symptoms via msCCA
